episodeTitle.en: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何讲好故事 | 马修·迪克斯（Storyworthy）

guestBioOfficial.en: Matthew Dicks is a best-selling author, columnist, blogger, podcaster, playwright, and teacher. He wrote my all-time favorite book on storytelling, Storyworthy. He is an elementary school teacher by day and by night teaches storytelling and public speaking to individuals, corporations, universities, religious institutions, and school districts around the world. He’s taught storytelling at Yale, MIT, Harvard, and Purdue, along with Amazon, Salesforce, Slack, Lego, and others. In this conversation, Matthew shares insights and techniques for effective storytelling, including: • The benefits of good storytelling in business
guestBioOfficial.zh: 马修·迪克斯（Matthew Dicks）是一位畅销书作家、专栏作家、博主、播客主、剧作家和教师。他写了一本我最喜欢的讲故事书籍《值得讲述的故事》（Storyworthy）。白天他是小学教师，晚上则为世界各地的个人、企业、大学、宗教机构和学区教授讲故事和公开演讲技巧。他曾在耶鲁大学、麻省理工学院、哈佛大学和普渡大学授课，同时与亚马逊、Salesforce、Slack、乐高等公司合作。在本次对话中，马修分享了有效讲故事的见解和技巧，包括：• 商业中良好讲故事的益处

title.en: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)
title.zh: 如何讲好故事 | 马修·迪克斯（Storyworthy）

summary.en: Matthew argues businesspeople love calling themselves storytellers but rarely separate from the herd, which makes them forgettable. He shows that stories - not charts or platitudes - are what human minds actually remember. The episode is a practical, energetic guide to using storytelling to be remembered and influential.
summary.zh: 马修指出，商界人士喜欢自称"讲故事的人"，却很少从人群中脱颖而出，结果变得容易被遗忘。他说明，人脑真正记住的是故事，而非图表或套话。本期是一份实用而充满能量的指南，教你用故事让人记住、产生影响。
